newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian real trades shade higher in placid mkt.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian real trades shade higher in placid mkt.

text.p: Brazil's real currency opened slightly lower, but quickly recovered to trade a sliver higher at mid-morning against the dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, traders said.
The real was up 0.02 percent at 1.0806 in average volume.
"The market appears to be calm so far," a currency trader at a large foreign bank said.

Brazil's spot foreign exchange market has been the calm in the eye of a storm over the past three sessions, as the Sao Paulo stock exchange was racked by currency woes in Asian emerging nations. Stocks had fallen 12 percent over the past few days, but recouped around four percent this morning.
Players are closely watching Brazilian currency markets for any signs of pressure on the real either by local or foreign currency speculators. So far, none has materialized.
But the real has rarely been the object of speculative attack, as the Central Bank has staunchly defended its mini-bands and has $59 billion in reserve muscle to back up its stance.
According to Central Bank data, net capital flows on Tuesday showed a surplus of $183 million and a surplus of $1.5 billion for the month to July 15.
In the futures market, August dollar contracts dropped 0.07 percent to trade at 1.08485 against the real.
